decision: scoped the port: 100 Python files, 17.8k lines, 15+ formats, 9 exporters, 3 TTS engines, 3 OCR backends
why: needed the size before planning a long run

decision: tried wxDragon first because it mirrors wxPython 1:1
why: least drift from the Python GUI
result: rejected: needs libclang + cmake + 20-min C++ wxWidgets build, libclang absent

decision: picked winsafe (native Win32 controls) and probed it
why: same native controls wx used, pure Rust build, direct HWND access for NotifyWinEvent and RichEdit
result: VERIFIED: tree, button, RichEdit, status bar expose correct MSAA roles

decision: built an MSAA audit script after the managed UIA client showed every Win32 control as an anonymous Pane
why: NVDA and JAWS read Win32 controls through MSAA, so audit what they see
result: caught tree and RichEdit with no name

decision: name unlabelled controls with IAccPropServices SetHwndPropStr
why: the documented Win32 way to set an accessible name, and the port of wx SetName
result: VERIFIED: audit PASS after the fix

decision: PDF via pdfium-render + lopdf, pdfium chromium/7881 bundled in vendor/
why: pdfium-render reads text/TOC/forms and writes text/checkbox/radio values; lopdf covers /TU and choice values
Surya is a Python ML model with no Rust port; Windows OCR is local, built in, high quality

decision: wrote shared contracts and compiling stubs for every module before fan-out
why: parallel agents must not edit the same files or invent their own types
result: cargo build ok, 4 unit tests pass

decision: built a parity harness that runs Prism's own Python handler and InTome's on the same file and scores text similarity
why: lets every format agent prove parity against the original instead of trusting a summary
result: red baseline: .txt stub fails as expected
